title: An inflammatory cytokine signature predicts COVID-19 severity and survival

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《An inflammatory cytokine signature predicts COVID-19 severity and survival》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Several studies have revealed that the hyper-inflammatory response induced by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is a major cause of disease severity and death.

evidence.text: Several studies have revealed that the hyper-inflammatory response induced by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is a major cause of disease severity and death.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《An inflammatory cytokine signature predicts COVID-19 severity and survival》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】We implemented a rapid multiplex cytokine assay to measure serum interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α and IL-1β in hospitalized patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) upon admission to the Mount Sinai Health System in New York.

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】Patients (n = 1,484) were followed up to 41 d after admission (median, 8 d), and clinical information, laboratory test results and patient outcomes were collected.

evidence.text: We implemented a rapid multiplex cytokine assay to measure serum interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α and IL-1β in hospitalized patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) upon admission to the Mount Sinai Health System in New York.
Patients (n = 1,484) were followed up to 41 d after admission (median, 8 d), and clinical information, laboratory test results and patient outcomes were collected.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《An inflammatory cytokine signature predicts COVID-19 severity and survival》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】We found that high serum IL-6, IL-8 and TNF-α levels at the time of hospitalization were strong and independent predictors of patient survival (P < 0.0001, P = 0.0205 and P = 0.0140, respectively).

evidence.text: We found that high serum IL-6, IL-8 and TNF-α levels at the time of hospitalization were strong and independent predictors of patient survival (P < 0.0001, P = 0.0205 and P = 0.0140, respectively).
